speaker: Patient
text: 31-year-old female. The patient reports experiencing chronic diarrhea on most days for the past four months. She mentions lower abdominal discomfort and cramping, which is relieved by diarrhea. The patient notes the bowel movements are urgent, occasionally accompanied by mucus discharge, and often followed by a feeling of incomplete evacuation. She went camping several months ago and recalls another member of the camping party falling ill recently.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Irritable Bowel Syndrome (IBS) with Diarrhea-Predominant (IBS-D).

The symptoms of chronic diarrhea, cramping relieved by defecation, urgency, and feeling of incomplete evacuation for four months are classic for IBS. While the camping history could suggest an infectious etiology like Giardia, the chronicity and specific relief pattern strongly point to a functional disorder.

I will proceed with this diagnosis based on the clinical presentation. If symptoms persist or worsen, a stool study for parasites would be appropriate.
